newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar steady in directionless Tokyo trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar steady in directionless Tokyo trade.

text.p: 0115 GMT -- *Dollar capped at around 114.80 yen in mid-morning Tokyo due to talk of offers by trust banks, and selling orders from Japanese exporters lining up to 115.40 yen.*If dollar can rise above 114.80 yen it may ride a gradual upward trend with stop-loss buying seen at around 115.00 yen. *Downside becoming solid after Japan's weak industrial production data last Friday, with bids detected at 114.20 yen.
*Stop-loss buying also seen at 1.7450 marks, but profit-taking inhibited its rise, dealers added.

*Some traders expect dollar to rise slowly, helped by strength in dollar/mark and expectations of upbeat U.S. economic data, even if the Federal Reserve decides to keep interest rates steady at their meeting starting later today.
*But many traders are not enthusiastic about pushing dollar strongly in either direction amid lack of fresh factors.
*Dollar steady against yen in early Tokyo after earlier firming on purchases by overseas operators.
*But exporters quick to sell greenback on topside, capping dollar's gains.
*"Since dollar/mark remained strong, we wanted to see an upward bias in dollar/yen. But exporters were quick to sell dollars (this morning)," the city bank dealer said.
*"We basically expect no policy changes in U.S. interest rates at the FOMC," a trust bank dealer said.

*But the city bank dealer said that strong U.S. data released on Monday would keep the market watching moves in U.S. market interest rates closely. If National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) survey on Tuesday also shows strength, this could fuel speculation about a U.S. credit-tightening in August or September, he added.
